explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - CheckCle is a full-stack, open-source monitoring platform.  
   - It comprises a React+TypeScript single-page application (SPA) in the **application/** folder and a PocketBase backend (Go) in the **server/** folder.  
   - Docker Compose glues everything together for local development and production.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top level:  
     • **application/** – the Vite-powered React SPA  
     • **server/** – PocketBase binary, migration scripts, SQLite data  
     • **docker/** + **docker-compose.yml** – container definitions for dev/prod  
     • **scripts/** – setup/entrypoint shell scripts
   - In **application/**:  
     • **src/pages/** implements route-level views (Dashboard, Login, Settings, etc.)  
     • **src/components/** holds UI components (dashboard, services, profile, settings, ssl-domain)  
     • **src/services/** contains API wrappers (authService, serviceService, etc.), monitoring logic (httpChecker, monitoring intervals), notification logic (telegramService, signalService, templateProcessor)  
     • **src/api/** configures REST + real-time (WebSocket) communication with PocketBase  
     • **src/lib/pocketbase.ts** – initializes the PocketBase SDK client  
     • **vite.config.ts**, **tsconfig.json**, **tailwind.config.ts** – build tool and styling configs  
   - In **server/**:  
     • **pb_data/** – SQLite files for data persistence  
     • **pb_migrations/** – JSON and JS migration scripts defining collections (services, uptimes, alert configurations)  
     • **pocketbase/** – the backend executable

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Real-time monitoring of HTTP, DNS, Ping, TCP services  
   - Incident history, SSL/domain checks, user and alert management  
   - Notification channels: Email, Telegram, Discord, Slack  
   - Multi-language, theming, and a settings panel  
   - Deployed via Docker Compose, exposing port 8090

4. How to create the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
      • Frontend SPA (React+Vite)  
      • Backend API & database (PocketBase + SQLite)  
      • Monitoring engine (schedules checks, httpChecker, ping, DNS)  
      • Notification engine (Telegram, Email, Slack integrations)  
      • External services (Telegram Bot API, SMTP/Discord/Slack)  
      • Docker Compose orchestration  
   b. Relationships & interactions  
      1. SPA ↔ REST API (CRUD services, user auth, settings)  
      2. SPA ↔ WebSocket (real-time uptime/status updates)  
      3. Monitoring engine → DB (write uptime results & incident records)  
      4. Monitoring engine → Notification engine → External channels  
      5. SPA subscribes to DB changes via WebSocket and displays updated metrics  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
      – Modular component hierarchy in the frontend (pages, components, hooks)  
      – Single-page application with real-time data via WebSocket  
      – PocketBase as a BaaS: REST + Realtime + built-in auth  
      – Separation of concerns: monitoring logic and notification logic decoupled from UI  
      – Docker Compose for environment consistency and data persistence  
   d. Key technologies  
      – React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS (frontend)  
      – PocketBase, SQLite (backend/DB)  
      – Docker, Docker Compose (deployment)  
      – WebSocket for real-time updates  
      – Telegram Bot API, SMTP, Slack Webhooks (notifications)

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack app  
   – Draw the **Frontend** box on the left, subdivided into Pages, Components, Services modules  
   – Draw the **Backend** box on the right, subdivided into PocketBase API, SQLite DB, Migration scripts  
   – Illustrate the **Monitoring Engine** as a separate service (it could run inside the PocketBase container or its own Node container)—show its schedule and HTTP/DNS/Ping check modules  
   – Show the **Notification Engine** next to the Monitoring Engine, with connectors to external channels  
   – Surround everything with the **Docker Compose** layer and annotate ports, volumes (pb_data)  

6. Elements to include in the diagram  
   – Clear, descriptive labels for each component  
   – Directional arrows showing:  
     • SPA → API calls → PocketBase  
     • API → DB reads/writes  
     • Monitoring Engine → DB writes  
     • Monitoring Engine → Notification Engine → External Channel  
     • DB → WebSocket pushes → SPA  
   – Color coding or distinct shapes:  
     • UI (blue),  
     • Backend/core services (green),  
     • External dependencies (orange),  
     • Data store (cylinder icon for SQLite)  
   – Annotations for protocols (HTTP, WebSocket, Docker network)

7. Final tips  
   – Be exhaustive: break out sub-modules (e.g., ServicesTable, RealTimeUpdates hook) only if it aids understanding.  
   – Capture all “moving parts”: frontend layers, API layer, scheduling layer, database, external channels.  
   – Use a tool like Lucidchart, draw.io, or Mermaid for clarity.  
   – Keep the diagram legible—avoid overcrowding.  

With these guidelines, the system design diagram will faithfully represent CheckCle’s architecture, making it clear how data flows from scheduled checks all the way to the user’s dashboard and notification channels.  
</explanation>
